shows_up_as: The cohort chart shows net dollar retention, so upgrades cover lost customers; customers who leave in the first weeks are dropped from the cohort size; the newest cohorts are missing or the best cohorts are shown alone.
mechanical_check: Rebuild cohorts from the revenue-by-customer export. Compare each cohort's starting count with the count in the model's cohort tab. Compute gross retention (each customer's later MRR capped at its starting MRR) beside net retention. Compare both with the deck's number. Check the a16z test that newer cohorts do better than older ones.
needs_model_reading: Reading a footnote such as 'active after onboarding' and judging whether the exclusion is fair; reading a chart that exists only as an image in the deck.

flag: Revenue counted as ARR when it is not recurring
shows_up_as: ARR includes a pilot, one-time fees, professional services, or a signed contract that has not gone live; MRR is multiplied by 12 from an all-in month.
mechanical_check: Tag each line of the ARR build by product type using the revenue export (subscription, pilot, onboarding, services). Recompute ARR from subscription lines only. Flag any ARR line whose contract is under 12 months or can end on short notice.
needs_model_reading: Reading the contract: is a pilot, an evaluation or an opt-out clause present, and does the customer owe anything after the first term.

flag: Burn does not match the hiring plan
shows_up_as: The model's payroll line grows by a few hires while the hiring plan lists many more, or the plan's start dates are earlier than the model uses. The deck's runway comes from the lighter model.
mechanical_check: Build monthly payroll from the hiring plan: base pay times a loaded-cost factor, from each start month. Compare it with the model's payroll line and the cash tab. Recompute runway from cash and net burn. Compare it with the deck.
needs_model_reading: Reading start dates or comp notes that sit in text (offer letters, assumptions notes); judging whether the loaded-cost factor is fair.

flag: Numbers disagree between the deck and the model
shows_up_as: The same ARR, customer count or margin appears with different values in the deck, the model, the metrics export and what the founder says on video.
mechanical_check: Pull labeled numbers from the deck's claims page and from named cells in the model and exports. Match by label and period. Flag any pair that differs by more than a set tolerance.
needs_model_reading: Matching 'customers' on a slide to 'logos' or 'paying accounts' in the model; spotting a different date or definition behind the same label; reading a number spoken on video.

shows_up_as: One customer or one group of locations makes up a large share of MRR while the deck says the base is spread out.
mechanical_check: From revenue by customer: top-one and top-three share of MRR. Compare with the deck's claim. Flag when the computed share is above the deck claim, or above a set line (MicroVentures calls 20 percent a common rule of thumb; a16z gives the definition and no line, so the line is a setting).
needs_model_reading: Reading the big customer's contract for renewal date and termination rights, which decide how risky the share is.

flag: Gross margin leaves out hosting or support cost
shows_up_as: Cost of revenue holds only some delivery costs. Hosting, model inference and support staff sit under R&D or sales.
mechanical_check: Recompute gross margin with every ledger line tagged as hosting, inference, telephony, or support included. Compare with the deck. Use benchmarks as context only: Bessemer's average is 65 to 70 percent with a middle half of 60 to 80, while a16z says software should sit at 80 to 90.
needs_model_reading: Classifying ambiguous ledger lines such as 'platform costs' or 'customer experience salaries'.

flag: Vanity metric: cumulative sign-ups shown as active users
shows_up_as: A count that can only rise (accounts created, downloads, total users ever) is shown as active customers.
mechanical_check: Test whether the deck's number equals the last value of a cumulative column. Test the column for never decreasing. Compare with the active or paying count in the metrics export.
needs_model_reading: Reading a chart or label that does not say what 'users' means.
